message: GOD RULE 2 violation: All 10 Verus proofs define local types (TimerGeneration, PendingTimerModel, TimerAuthorityModel, TimerKindModel, NodeKindModel, TimerSlot, PendingTimerState, CommandQueueModel) and prove properties about these local models. No extern_spec binding to production types from vb_runtime::shard. No requires/ensures on any production exec fn. Zero use of production imports. Each proof fn proves properties of its own file-local types — the verifier would succeed even if production code were absent. This is the exact anti-pattern: prove properties of an enum defined in verification/verus/ and call it a day.
required_fix: Either add extern_spec blocks binding spec models to production types (vb_runtime::shard::PendingTimer, TimerWheel) with requires/ensures on production exec fn, prove bisimulation between local model and production code, or remove Verus obligations with compensating Kani+Proptest coverage.

message: Loom models improved from attempt 1 (now Arc<Mutex<...>>, multi-threaded, meaningful interleavings) but all use locally-defined data types (TimerEntry, TimerWheelModel, TimerAuthority, TimerState) instead of wrapping production types from vb_runtime::shard. While Loom requires loom-specific primitives, the model should either import production types and loom-wrap their shared fields, or document a formal bisimulation between model and production structures.
required_fix: Either wrap production data types in loom primitives for shared fields, document formal structural correspondence with bisimulation justification, or waive Loom obligations with compensating Kani+Proptest+Miri evidence.

message: All 46 artifacts marked PENDING_FORMAL_EXECUTION. Proof-reviewer rule 9 requires cheap smoke/typecheck evidence. No verus parse/typecheck output, no cargo kani compilation check, no cargo test compilation check, no verifier tool version report captured under .evidence/.
required_fix: Run each artifact through at least compilation/typecheck with stdout/stderr captured under .evidence/.

message: Kani harnesses violate workspace engineering rules ('no unwrap, expect, panic'). PS-001-harness.rs:16 uses entry.unwrap().generation. PS-001-harness.rs:27 uses wheel.get_entry(run).unwrap().generation. PS-007-harness.rs:12-13,27-28,41-42 use wheel.insert(...).unwrap(). In Kani, unwrap on proven-Some may be safe but project rules are zero-tolerance.
required_fix: Replace all .unwrap() with match/if-let patterns or assert!(result.is_ok())+result.ok() accessor patterns.

message: Flux files now contain actual #[flux_rs::sig] attributes (improvement from attempt 1) but use #[trusted] heavily: PS-002 has 3/3 functions trusted (initial_generation, matches_authority_except_deadline, timer_step_raw). PS-001 has SafeGeneration impl+functions all trusted. When all functions are #[trusted], Flux becomes documentation, not verification. Each trusted marker lacks a ledger entry explaining why it cannot be verified.
required_fix: Reduce #[trusted] usage: prove simple functions (initial_generation returns 1). Limit to genuinely opaque boundaries. Add per-trusted ledger entries.
